key_dates.label: Six models removed from all GitHub Copilot experiences

sources.title: GitHub Changelog: Upcoming deprecation of selected GitHub Copilot models in December

items.headline: GitHub Copilot retires six models on Dec 14, including Claude Fable 5 and Gemini 3.8 Flash
items.summary: GitHub will remove Claude Fable 5, Claude Haiku 4.5, Gemini 3.8 Flash, Gemini 4 Argon, Grok 4.6 and Kimi K3 from every Copilot experience on Dec 14, 2026. Suggested replacements are Fable 5.2, Haiku 5.5, Gemini 4 Hydrogen, Gemini 4 Carbon and Grok 4.7; Kimi K3's replacement is still to be announced.
items.curriculum_note: Check every Copilot lab, setup guide and screenshot that names one of these models and switch it to the replacement before cohorts hit Dec 14.
details: For Copilot Business and Enterprise, replacement models are enabled automatically unless an admin turned off the global default or disabled the model; in that case admins must enable them in the model policies.
Claude Haiku 4.5 stays available to individual subscribers on annual plans.
No action is needed to remove the retired models; they disappear on the date.

sources.title: Anthropic: Claude Code CHANGELOG
OpenAI: ChatGPT and Codex changelog
gradually.ai: Claude Code changelog with release dates

items.headline: Claude Code and Codex tighten agent defaults: sandboxed commands prompt again, untrusted folders lose MCP
items.summary: Claude Code 2.1.325 makes sandboxed Bash commands follow the normal permission prompts by default; teams that want the old no-prompt behavior must set sandbox.autoAllowBashIfSandboxed to true. Codex CLI 0.169.0 keeps project configuration and MCP servers disabled when codex exec runs in an untrusted directory, with --trust to save trust explicitly.
items.curriculum_note: Update agent setup guides so students see the new prompts, and teach why a coding agent should not load a repo's own config or MCP servers before the folder is trusted.
details: Claude Code 2.1.321 also fixed MCP OAuth requests that could send refresh tokens to another host after a redirect.
Claude Code 2.1.323 added Code Mode, an experimental opt-in where Claude writes JavaScript to call its tools, and an engines version range in plugin.json.
Codex CLI 0.168.0 and 0.169.0 (both Nov 13) also let teams add custom model providers and gateways from the terminal.
Claude Code's changelog gives no dates; the Nov 9 to 13 release dates come from a third-party changelog mirror.

sources.title: Google: Introducing Gemini 4 Hydrogen
GitHub Changelog: Gemini 4 Hydrogen in GitHub Copilot

items.headline: Gemini 4 Hydrogen becomes Google's fast, cheap agent model at $1.50 and $7.50 per million tokens
items.summary: Gemini 4 Hydrogen (gemini-4-hydrogen) is the fast tier of Gemini 4, with a 1M-token context window and a flat price of $1.50 per million input tokens and $7.50 per million output tokens. Google says it finishes tasks about 2.5 times faster than Gemini 3.8 Flash and adds a new xhigh thinking level. It is in the Gemini API, AI Studio, Antigravity, the Gemini app and Search.
items.curriculum_note: Add Hydrogen to the model-tiering lesson as the default for high-volume agent steps, with Carbon kept for the hard planning steps.
details: Google reports 57% on Terminal-Bench 4.1 versus 18.2% for Gemini 3.8 Flash, and more than five times fewer fabricated claims. Vendor numbers.
Antigravity's orchestrator can switch between Carbon and Hydrogen within one session; Google reports near-Carbon results with 24% less quota used.
Thinking levels: low, medium, high (default) and the new xhigh. The post does not mention Vertex AI or any retirement dates.
GitHub made Hydrogen generally available in Copilot on Nov 13.

sources.title: Claude: Operate Claude Managed Agents inside your security perimeter
Claude Platform release notes

items.headline: Claude Managed Agents can now run entirely inside a customer's own infrastructure
items.summary: Anthropic opened a private beta of self-hosted Claude Managed Agents: the customer runs the harness, sandboxes, credentials and session history in its own cloud or on-premise, and picks where model requests go (Anthropic, Bedrock, Google's Agent Platform, Microsoft Foundry or its own gateway). Access is through the Anthropic account team.
items.curriculum_note: A good case for the deployment-architecture module: compare hosted, sandbox-only self-hosted and fully self-hosted agents on data location, credentials and audit.
details: Credentials sit in a proxy outside the sandbox and can live in the customer's own secrets manager; each environment can be limited to an allowlist of hosts.
Every session is recorded and can be exported over OpenTelemetry; session history is stored in the customer's database.
Earlier, only the sandboxes could be self-hosted; the agent loop stayed with Anthropic.

sources.title: EU Publications Office: C/2026/6005, Article 50 guidelines
CASRAI: Article 50 guidelines published (news summary)

items.headline: EU publishes its Article 50 transparency guidelines in the Official Journal
items.summary: The Commission's guidelines on the AI Act's Article 50 transparency duties appeared as Communication C/2026/6005, dated Nov 12, 2026. They cover telling people they are talking to an AI system, machine-readable marking of AI-generated content, and labeling deepfakes. The guidelines are not binding but are the reference regulators will use.
items.curriculum_note: Cite C/2026/6005 as the reference in the EU transparency lesson, in place of the draft guidelines from May.
details: Article 50 duties have applied since Aug 2, 2026; the Commission had posted the guidelines on its own site in July.
The Publications Office record lists the document and date; its full text was not read for this brief.

sources.title: Google: Gemini Decisions API

items.headline: Google's Gemini Decisions API scores fixed choices in one pass for routing, tool selection and policy checks
items.summary: Gemini Decision 1 (gemini-decision-1) answers closed-set questions, such as yes or no, multiple choice or rubric scores, with probabilities and a confidence score instead of generated text. It costs $0.10 per million input tokens with free output, handles up to 1,000 questions per request, and Google reports 150 to 250 ms latency.
items.curriculum_note: Use it as a worked example of a model router: send low-confidence decisions to a larger model or a human, and log the confidence score.
details: Input can be text, images, audio, video and PDFs up to 256K tokens; shared input is billed once per request.
Google says Gemini Notebook uses it for model routing and Search uses it as a safety layer for MCP tools.
Available in the Gemini API and AI Studio; Google Cloud support is listed as coming soon. Integrations with LangChain, LiteLLM, Pydantic AI, Vercel and others are rolling out.

sources.title: United: United Restricts Access for Third-Party AI Agents

items.headline: United Airlines restricts third-party AI agents from booking and managing reservations
items.summary: United is restricting unauthorized third-party personal AI agents on its own platforms and indirectly through travel agencies and aggregators, and is updating its booking, ticketing and distribution policies. It cites credential sharing, unintended purchases or account changes, and FAA and DOT rules that need a human, such as check-in.
items.curriculum_note: Use this in agent design reviews: an agent that acts on a third-party site needs that site's permission, its own identity and a human step where rules require one, not the user's shared password.
details: United says banks and retailers have taken similar steps and encourages others to follow.
The release gives no effective date or technical detail on how the restriction is enforced.

key_dates.label: Gemini 4 Carbon introductory API price ends; price doubles

sources.title: Google: Gemini 4 Carbon is now available
GitHub Changelog: Gemini 4 Carbon in GitHub Copilot

items.headline: Gemini 4 Carbon opens to paying developers, and its API price doubles after Nov 30
items.summary: Google's strongest model, Gemini 4 Carbon (gemini-4-carbon), is now available through Google AI Studio and Gemini for business at an introductory $2 per million input tokens and $10 per million output tokens. After Nov 30, 2026 it costs $4 and $20. Google still recommends Gemini 4 Argon for most software engineering work and positions Carbon for harder, long-horizon and security tasks.
items.curriculum_note: If any lab or cost exercise uses Carbon, budget at the post-Nov 30 price, and use Carbon versus Hydrogen as the live example of picking a tier per task.
details: Also rolling out to Google AI Ultra subscribers in the Gemini app, AI Mode in Search and Google Antigravity; a cyber variant is available through Google's Fairwind Program.
Google reports a 0.8% per-attempt breach rate in simulated attacks for Carbon versus 3.1% for Argon, and 92% versus 70% on an agentic honesty benchmark. These are the vendor's own numbers.
GitHub made Gemini 4 Carbon generally available in Copilot the same day for Pro+, Max, Business and Enterprise plans.

sources.title: MCP blog: Exploring File Uploads and Downloads in MCP

items.headline: MCP drafts an extension for moving files between clients and tools without passing them through the model
items.summary: The experimental io.modelcontextprotocol/files extension lets a server mark a tool argument as a file. The client sends metadata first, uploads the bytes directly over HTTPS if the server accepts, then repeats the call; downloads come back as targets the client fetches and verifies.
items.curriculum_note: Worth a demo in the MCP module once a reference implementation ships; for now, teach its credential rules as a pattern for safe file handling.
details: Each upload or download target says whether MCP credentials are omitted or included; clients must refuse redirects and targets that set their own Authorization header.
There is a draft spec but no reference implementation yet; the maintainers aim to stabilize it before the end of 2026. Servers and clients can ignore it.
Written by the lead maintainer with a Google co-author.

sources.title: Cognizant press release (PR Newswire, via Finviz)

items.headline: Cognizant puts more than 25,000 people into a Claude delivery group and will run Claude systems for clients
items.summary: Cognizant formed a Claude Frontier Capability Group of more than 25,000 people and launched a managed-services model in which it runs Claude-powered systems in production for clients. It reports more than 44,000 staff trained or certified on Claude.
items.curriculum_note: Shows where FDE work is heading: from build-and-hand-off to build-and-run. Add operating a deployed agent (monitoring, cost, incident response) to the capstone.
details: The release names new roles, Frontier Certified Engineers and Frontier Business Operators, credentialed by model companies; it does not use the term forward deployed engineer.
Cognizant says it holds more than 26,000 Claude certifications.
Pitched to clients as more predictable AI spend with enterprise security and governance controls.

sources.title: Claude: Your apps can now open in Claude, and Claude can work in them
Claude: Introducing Claude Whiteboards, Claude Sheets, and Claude Data

items.headline: Claude adds interactive connectors built on MCP Apps, plus Sheets, Whiteboards and Data
items.summary: Interactive connectors open a live view of a tool such as Asana, Canva, Dropbox or monday.com inside Claude, where Claude can make changes the user approves. They run on MCP Apps, an open MCP extension, so the same app can work in other AI clients. Claude Sheets, Whiteboards and Data launched the same day.
items.curriculum_note: Add an MCP Apps example to the MCP module, since customers will now expect a tool's own interface inside the assistant, not only text tool calls.
details: Developer support for building interactive connectors is in public preview.
Rolling out on web and desktop on all plans; admins restrict a connector's tools the same way as before.

key_dates.label: Large frontier AI developers must register through New York's RAISE Portal

sources.title: Governor of New York: launch of RAISE Portal and research center
TechCrunch: New York's AI safety law takes effect

items.headline: New York opens RAISE Act registration; large frontier developers must register by Jan 1, 2027
items.summary: New York's DIGIT office opened the RAISE Portal, where large frontier AI developers must register by Jan 1, 2027. Frontier developers must report critical safety incidents within 72 hours and publish model transparency reports, and large developers must publish safety frameworks starting in January. The state also launched a research center at SUNY Binghamton to test advanced AI systems.
items.curriculum_note: Few trainees will build frontier models, but their customers will ask about vendors' incident reporting; add RAISE to the vendor due-diligence checklist next to California's SB 53.
details: The Department of Financial Services leads implementation through the DIGIT office.
TechCrunch reports penalties of up to $1 million per violation and $3 million for later ones; the governor's release does not mention penalties.

sources.title: Meta: Muse Ember model page
Mad Robot: Meta's Muse Ember (news report, Nov 9)

items.headline: Meta releases Muse Ember, a small 1M-context model priced for high-volume agent steps
items.summary: Muse Ember (muse-ember-1.0) is Meta's smallest multimodal reasoning model, priced at $0.10 per million input tokens and $0.50 per million output tokens up to 200K context. Meta pitches it for tool calls, coding subtasks, routing and extraction, paired with larger Muse models for planning.
items.curriculum_note: Another option for the cheap-executor role in multi-model agent labs; compare it on cost with Hydrogen and Haiku.
details: Available through Meta's Model API, OpenRouter and Google Cloud Marketplace.
Meta's own benchmark table shows it ahead of Claude Haiku 5.5 and GPT-6 Luna on most listed tests but behind Haiku 5.5 on FrontierCode 2.0.
Meta's model page gives no release date; Nov 9 comes from news coverage.

sources.title: MCP release cycle post

items.headline: MCP moves to two specification releases a year
items.summary: Spec versions now ship on a six-month schedule, generally the last Tuesday of March and September. The next release is planned for March 30, 2027 as version 2027-03-30. The maintainers say existing clients and servers need no changes because of this announcement.
items.curriculum_note: Pin MCP labs to the spec version the SDKs target today, and put a lab refresh on the calendar for April 2027.
details: Planning for each release starts eight months ahead, with proposal deadlines and SDK beta dates published in advance.
The change affects how releases are prepared, not MCP messages or version negotiation.

items.date_note: Image deprecation posted Nov 10; cyber preview removal posted Nov 5.

sources.title: OpenAI API deprecations

items.headline: OpenAI sets February shutdowns for gpt-image-2 and the cyber preview model
items.summary: gpt-image-2 and gpt-image-2-2026-04-21 shut down on Feb 10, 2027, with gpt-image-2.6-sunburst or gpt-image-2.6-flare as replacements. gpt-5.5-cyber-preview is removed on Feb 1, 2027.
items.curriculum_note: Find any lab or demo that calls gpt-image-2 and migrate it before Feb 10. Use this as the live example in the lesson on watching vendor deprecation pages.
details: The image deprecation was posted Nov 10; the cyber preview removal was posted Nov 5.
For the cyber model, OpenAI's guidance is to move to the most capable cyber model available to your account.

sources.title: Introducing Claude Fable 5.2 and Claude Mythos 5.2

items.headline: Claude Fable 5.2 becomes the new top tier, with Mythos 5.2 for vetted security and life-science teams
items.summary: Anthropic released Claude Fable 5.2 (API id claude-fable-5-2) on all major clouds at $8 per million input tokens and $40 per million output tokens, or $16 and $80 in fast mode. Mythos 5.2 is the same underlying model with lighter cyber and biology restrictions, available only through Anthropic's verification programs. Anthropic still recommends starting most work on its current Opus model and moving up to Fable or down to Sonnet or Haiku as needed.
items.curriculum_note: Teach model tiering as a cost decision: run the same agent task on two tiers and have students justify the escalation with the price difference.
details: Anthropic reports SWE v2 at 69.9% for Fable 5.2 against 62.3% for its current Opus model. These are the vendor's own numbers.
The post describes Fable 5.2 building a prototype operating system over eight days with more than 1,000 subagents.
Preserved thinking now applies to every API account, so integrations that handle thinking blocks should be checked.

sources.title: NIST IR 8621

items.headline: NIST names the gaps in incident response for AI agents
items.summary: NIST IR 8621 reports on a workshop of more than 400 experts. It finds that traditional monitoring can miss prompt injection, shifts in model behavior and unauthorized agent actions. Priorities include reasoning-layer telemetry, governance of non-human identities, and containment scoped to what an agent is allowed to do.
items.curriculum_note: Add an agent incident drill: students trace a prompt-injection incident through tool logs, then revoke the agent's credentials without taking down the whole app.
details: Planned follow-ups include an update to SP 800-61 for AI-related incidents and a NIST AI Consortium task group on agent monitoring and containment.
For procurement, NIST notes vendors often hold key records, so contracts should cover audit rights, incident notification and evidence.

sources.title: The evolution of forward-deployed engineering

items.headline: Microsoft's FDE lead says the unit of deployment is now a pod, and the goal is handoff
items.summary: Kevin Shatzkamer, CVP of Forward Deployed Engineering, writes that the role has widened from embedded engineering to end-to-end delivery, done by small multidisciplinary pods rather than a lone expert. Projects should leave the customer able to run the system, not dependent on the FDE team.
items.curriculum_note: Run the capstone as a pod with named roles, and grade the handoff package (runbook, architecture notes, named customer owner) alongside the demo.
details: Skills named as mattering now: multi-agent systems, tool use through MCP, evaluations, observability, identity and security, state management, cost and latency, CI/CD, and AI-assisted development.
"The common denominator remains hands-on engineering embedded close to the customer's real work."

sources.title: Gibson Dunn: Europe data protection update

items.headline: Spain requires employers to explain algorithmic decisions to workers in writing
items.summary: Spain's data protection authority issued guidance on Royal Decree 723/2026, which requires employers to inform workers in writing about algorithmic decision-making systems. GDPR duties still apply alongside it, and the note warns about tools that screen and rank job candidates.
items.curriculum_note: A useful case study for any cohort building candidate screening or ranking: the same tool carries different notice duties in Colorado and Spain.
details: Read through Gibson Dunn's October data protection roundup; the regulator's own note was not opened for this sample.

items.date_note: Guidance published Jul 27, 2026; reporting duties live since Sep 11, 2026.

key_dates.label: EU Cyber Resilience Act main obligations apply

sources.title: European Commission: Cyber Resilience Act guidance

items.headline: Cyber Resilience Act reporting duties are already live
items.summary: Manufacturers of products with digital elements sold in the EU have had reporting obligations since Sep 11, 2026. The main obligations apply from Dec 11, 2027. The Commission's non-binding guidance covers scope, substantial modification, support periods, reporting and risk assessment, with 67 worked examples.
items.curriculum_note: When an FDE ships software to an EU customer, include vulnerability reporting and a stated support period in the release checklist.
details: The guidance also addresses remote data processing and free and open source software.

sources.title: Forward Deployed Engineering for Partners

items.headline: AWS partner FDE teams must clear a technical bar and own a reusable delivery harness
items.summary: AWS's partner-led FDE program asks consulting partners to field AWS-credentialed teams that pass an AWS-defined technical bar before meeting customers. Each partner builds and owns a delivery harness: domain ontologies, evaluation frameworks, MCP servers, agent operations tooling, and a record of architecture decisions.
items.curriculum_note: Use the harness list as the cohort's definition of deployable: each team ships evals, an MCP server and an ops runbook, not only an agent.
details: AWS describes the bar as a production-engineering standard, not a certification checkbox.
The program extends AWS's $1 billion FDE investment announced the same day, where payment is tied to business results rather than billable hours.

sources.title: MeshLaw: US state AI laws in 2026 (Sep 22, 2026)

items.headline: Colorado's rewritten AI law takes effect Jan 1, 2027
items.summary: SB 26-189 repeals and replaces the 2024 Colorado AI Act, which never took effect. Developers and deployers of automated decision tools that materially influence consequential decisions owe notice before use, a plain-language explanation of an adverse decision within 30 days, and a path to human reconsideration and data correction.
items.curriculum_note: In hiring and HR tool scenarios, add notice, explanation and human-review steps to the FDE requirements checklist.
details: Signed May 14, 2026. The state Attorney General enforces it alone, with a 60-day cure period.
Developers must give deployers documentation about the tool.

items.date_note: Current release on the updates page, read Nov 13, 2026; the page gives no release date.

sources.title: VS Code updates

items.headline: VS Code runs Claude, Copilot and Codex agents side by side, and enterprises can lock down MCP servers
items.summary: A preview setting lets nested chat sessions use different agent harnesses next to each other, each with its own model and permission level. For servers VS Code starts, the enterprise allowedMcpServers list now takes precedence over registry-only access, and an empty list blocks every server.
items.curriculum_note: Add an exercise where students write an enterprise MCP allowlist using server URL and command rules, then confirm an unlisted server is blocked.
details: The setting is chat.agentHost.multipleChatProviders.enabled.
VS Code recommends serverUrl and serverCommand rules over serverName, which matches a label the server's author chooses.
Several tools were removed from Local agent sessions, and the Copilot harness stays the default for new sessions.

sources.title: White & Case: EU AI Omnibus enters into force
European Commission: Code of Practice on marking and labelling AI-generated content

items.headline: EU watermarking grace period ends Dec 2, 2026
items.summary: Under the AI Act amendments in Regulation (EU) 2026/1744, generative AI systems placed on the market before Aug 2, 2026 must meet the watermarking obligation by Dec 2, 2026. Newer systems have had to comply since Aug 2, and the other transparency duties in Article 50 also apply from that date. The Commission's voluntary Code of Practice on marking and labelling AI-generated content is the practical guide.
items.curriculum_note: Any demo app a cohort ships to EU users should mark generated content, label deepfakes, and tell users when they are talking to a chatbot.
details: The amending regulation entered into force July 27, 2026. It moved Annex III high-risk duties to Dec 2, 2027 and Annex I duties to Aug 2, 2028.
The AI literacy duty was softened: providers and deployers must take measures to support a sufficient level of AI literacy among staff.
